messages.subject: Multigroup CFA Measurement Equivalence Ordered Indicators
parts:
I am testing for measurement equivalence of a 6-factor measure across three languages (n in sample 1 = 450, n in sample 2 = 850; n in sample 3 = 1,100). Each factor of the measure has five indicators which are measured on a 4-point scale (0-3).

This is the model I specify:

rcads1<-'
DEPR=~dep1+dep2+dep3+dep4+dep5
PANIC=~p1+p2+p3+p4+p5
SOCAnx=~soc1+soc2+soc3+soc4+soc5
SEPAnx=~sad1+sad2+sad3+sad4+sad5
GenANX=~gad1+gad2+gad3+gad4+gad5
ObsCD=~ocd1+ocd2+ocd3+ocd4+ocd5' 

The model fits ok using each sample separately, so I test measurement equivalence using multigroup CFA with this code:

baseline <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = rcads1, data = all, ordered = vars, parameterization = "theta",
                          ID.fac = "std.lv", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",group = "sample",
                          group.equal = "configural")

threshold <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = rcads1, data = all, ordered = vars, parameterization = "theta",
                          ID.fac = "std.lv", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "sample",
                          group.equal = "thresholds")

loadings <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = rcads1,data = all,ordered = vars, parameterization = "theta",
                          ID.fac = "std.lv", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "sample",
                          group.equal = c("thresholds","loadings"))

residuals <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = rcads1,data = all,ordered = vars, parameterization = "theta",
                          ID.fac = "std.lv", ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016", group = "sample",
                          group.equal = c("thresholds","loadings","residuals"))

model.baseline <- as.character(baseline)
model.threshold <- as.character(threshold)
model.loadings <- as.character(loadings)
model.residuals <- as.character(residuals)

fit.baseline <- cfa(model.baseline, data = all, group = "sample", ordered = vars)
fit.threshold <- cfa(model.threshold, data = all, group = "sample", ordered = vars)
fit.loadings <- cfa(model.loadings, data = all, group = "sample", ordered = vars)
fit.residuals <- cfa(model.residuals, data = all, group = "sample", ordered = vars)

Below are fit indices for each model:
chisq.scaled  df.scaled pvalue.scaled  rmsea.scaled    cfi.scaled     tli.scaled       srmr 
3696.533       1170.000         0.000                0.055              0.936         0.929         0.062  Configural
3833.931       1230.000         0.000                0.055              0.934         0.930         0.062  Threshold
3699.587       1278.000         0.000                0.052              0.939         0.938         0.068  Loadings
3815.780       1338.000         0.000                0.051              0.938         0.939         0.068  Residuals

I am qurious about chisquared being lower in models 3 & 4 compared to model 2. 

Question 1. Does the code look ok?
Question 2. If yes, how can chisquared be lower in models 3 & 4 compared to model 2?

Thanks for a great package and for a great help page!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Multigroup CFA Measurement Equivalence Ordered Indicators
parts: Question 1. Does the code look ok?

Except for group.equal = "configural", which doesn't make any sense.  It won't break anything, but "configural" is not a type of parameter.  For the configural model, you would just leave out the group.equal= argument because you aren't constraining any parameters.
Question 2. If yes, how can chisquared be lower in models 3 & 4 compared to model 2?

You can't compare scaled/shifted chi-squared stats from different models.  The robust chi-squared difference test is calculated by scaling/shifting the difference between naive chi-squared stats from 2 nested models.  From your description, I can see you are gaining the correct number of degrees of freedom at each step, so I wouldn't worry about it.  To verify the models are nested, you could use the net() function.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

parts:
should I use the following code to examine the relative model fit and compare the chi-square statistics between the baseline model with the model where threshold equality constraints are employed?
lavTestLRT(fit.baseline,fit.threshold)
If "baseline" is your configural model, then yes.
Typically, you compare Step X to Step X-1 (so loadings to thresholds, then residuals to loadings), assuming you can't reject the H0 from the previous step.
